name: myNaturevista – Nature & Travel Widgets (Weather, Sunrise, Moon, Destinations)
author: mynaturevista

sections.description:
Weather, sunrise and sunset, moon phase, air quality and nature destination widgets for hotels, travel agencies and travel blogs.

This plugin connects your site to myNaturevista, where the widgets are designed, and shows them with a block or a shortcode. A free account is enough to start: no card needed.

Widgets included

  • Nature Explorer
  • Weather
  • Sunrise & Sunset
  • Moon Phase
  • Air Quality

How it works

  1. Connect your myNaturevista account from the plugin’s page. If you have none, you create it in that step.
  2. Your first widget is created for you, with example content, so you see it working at once.
  3. Add the “myNaturevista Widget” block to a page, or paste the shortcode, and publish.

You change a widget’s colours, texts and content in your myNaturevista dashboard, opened from the plugin with one click. Every page that shows the widget updates by itself: you do not edit the page again.

Why site owners like it

  • Each widget loads in its own frame: your theme cannot break it, and it cannot break your theme.
  • Works with the block editor, the classic editor, and page builders such as Elementor and Divi (through the shortcode).
  • The editor shows the real widget, and those previews are not counted as views.
  • Nothing is loaded on pages without a widget.

Free plan and paid plans

The Free plan includes three live widgets on one site and 1,000 widget views a month. Widgets on the Free plan show a small “Powered by myNaturevista” line, added by the service inside the widget. Paid plans remove it and raise the limits. All widgets are available on every plan. See the plans.

External services

This plugin relies on the myNaturevista service (https://mynaturevista.com). It is required: the widgets are created, stored and served by it.

Nothing is sent to the service until you connect your account from the plugin’s page.

  • When you connect, and while you use the plugin’s page or the block editor: your site’s address and the access you granted are sent from your server to mynaturevista.com, to link the site to your account, list your widgets, create new ones and read your plan’s usage.
  • When a visitor opens a page that shows a widget: the visitor’s browser loads the widget from mynaturevista.com. That request carries the visitor’s IP address (anonymised before it is stored), the address of the page and the browser’s user agent. They are used to show the widget and to count widget views.

Some widgets load data from other providers inside their own frame (weather and air quality data, map tiles, the media files you link). That happens in the service, not in this plugin.

Terms of service: https://mynaturevista.com/terms-of-service.html
Privacy policy: https://mynaturevista.com/privacy-policy.html
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Open myNaturevista in the admin menu and press Connect with myNaturevista.
  3. Add the myNaturevista Widget block to a page, or paste the shortcode shown next to each widget, for example [mynaturevista id="123"].
sections.faq:
Is it free?

Yes. The Free plan includes three live widgets on one site and 1,000 widget views a month. Paid plans raise the limits and remove the “Powered by myNaturevista” line.

Do I need an account?

Yes, a myNaturevista account. You can create it while connecting, for free.

Does it slow down my site?

Each widget loads lazily in its own frame after your page, and the loader is added only on pages that show a widget.

Can I use it with Elementor, Divi or the classic editor?

Yes. Paste the widget’s shortcode in a shortcode or text element.

Why does my widget show “Powered by myNaturevista”?

Widgets on the Free plan carry that line, added by the service inside the widget. Any paid plan removes it.

What happens when I reach my monthly views?

You are warned by email at 80% and at 100%, and the plugin’s page shows it too. Widgets keep showing up to 120%; beyond that they are hidden, leaving no gap on your pages, until the next month or until you upgrade.

The widget does not show on my site. Why?

Open the plugin’s page: it tells you if the site’s domain is not in your account, if the widget is hidden, or if your plan’s limits were reached. A widget only renders on the domain registered in your account.

Can I try it on a local or staging site?

On a local address (localhost, *.local, *.test) widgets show with a “Test mode” mark and their views are not counted.

I have another myNaturevista plugin installed. Do I connect twice?

No. The myNaturevista plugins share one connection and one settings page.
